title: Measuring for the New Lens

patient.name: Mdm Koh Siew Ling
patient.presenting_complaint: Booked for cataract surgery; here for biometry to calculate the lens implant power
patient.address: Blk 544 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #09-813, Singapore 166557

history.hpc: Mdm Koh is listed for right eye cataract surgery and attends for biometry. She says: 'Doctor say want to operate my cataract, must measure my eye for the lens.' Her cataract is moderate and she can still fixate. The OT must perform non-contact optical biometry, obtain reliable measurements, and document them for IOL power calculation.
history.social_hx: Lives with daughter. Non-smoker. Keen to proceed with surgery.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Moderate nuclear cataract right eye; media still permits optical biometry
examination_findings.fundus: For doctor as part of pre-op assessment

investigations.optical_biometry: Non-contact optical coherence biometry performed: axial length, corneal curvature (keratometry), and anterior chamber depth measured for the right (operative) eye, with the left eye for comparison. Multiple readings taken and checked for consistency; good fixation confirmed. Values documented for IOL power calculation.
investigations.measurement_quality: Readings consistent across repeats; fixation stable; no warning flags on the measurement.

diagnosis: Routine pre-cataract optical biometry to obtain axial length, keratometry, and anterior chamber depth for IOL power calculation. Optical (non-contact) biometry is the preferred method in most eyes and is more accurate than A-scan when the media allow. The OT competency is reliable measurement and documentation; the IOL choice is the doctor's.

immediate: Confirm the diagnosis/indication (cataract surgery) and which eye is to be operated
Explain the non-contact scan and position the patient with good fixation on the target
Acquire axial length, keratometry, and anterior chamber depth; take multiple readings and check consistency
Confirm there are no quality/warning flags before saving
Document diagnosis, indication, RE/LE, and the biometry values for IOL calculation
Hand the measurements to the doctor for IOL power selection (do not select the IOL)
follow_up: Doctor to calculate and select the IOL power from the biometry
Complete the rest of the pre-op assessment
Keep the measurements on file for the surgical plan
patient_education: Explain the scan is painless and non-contact, just looking at a light
Ask her to keep still and fixate to get accurate measurements
Explain the numbers are used to choose the correct lens implant power
Reassure her this is a routine step before cataract surgery

key_points: Confirms the indication (cataract surgery) and the operative eye
Confirms the patient can fixate and the media allow optical biometry
Checks relevant history before the measurement
Explains the procedure to gain cooperation
Performs non-contact optical biometry with good fixation
Acquires axial length, keratometry, and anterior chamber depth
Takes multiple readings and checks consistency/quality flags
Documents diagnosis, indication, RE/LE, and values for IOL calculation
Understands optical biometry is preferred and more accurate when media allow
Knows the measurements are for IOL power calculation
Recognises the need for consistent, quality-checked readings
Knows IOL selection is the doctor's role
Produces reliable, quality-checked biometry for the operative eye
Documents the values clearly for IOL calculation
Explains the scan to the patient and gains cooperation
Hands measurements to the doctor for IOL selection
